title: Chicken Shawarma
kicker: The vertical spit's greatest hits, adapted for a humble sheet pan — yogurt, turmeric, seven spices, one addictive garlic sauce.
story: Shawarma is a Levantine word for the vertical rotating spit — the Turkish döner's cousin — where marinated meat shaves off in crispy ribbons. Home ovens can't spin a spit, but a screaming-hot sheet pan gets close: thigh meat, deeply spiced, roasted until the edges blacken and caramelize.

Two components make it real. First, the marinade: yogurt tenderizes while turmeric, cumin, cardamom, allspice and a pinch of cinnamon take care of everything else — overnight is transformative, 4 hours acceptable. Second, toum, the Lebanese garlic sauce that is just garlic, oil, lemon and emulsion physics. Shawarma without toum is a jacket without sleeves.
fun_fact: Shawarma migrated to Mexico with Lebanese immigrants and became tacos al pastor — the world's most successful recipe diaspora, complete with the spit.

steps.title: Marinate overnight
steps.text: Whisk marinade, coat the thighs thoroughly, refrigerate at least 4 hours, best overnight. The yogurt works slowly; respect its schedule.

steps.title: Quick-pickle the onion
steps.text: Toss sliced onion with vinegar, sugar, salt. Thirty minutes turns it candy-pink and sharp-sweet. It keeps a week and improves everything it touches.

steps.title: Roast hot and hard
steps.text: Spread thighs in one layer on a foil-lined sheet pan. 230°C / 450°F for 25-30 minutes until edges char in spots. Rest 5 minutes, then slice thin across the grain — the shaved-ribbon look that makes it shawarma.

steps.title: Crisp the ribbons (optional, glorious)
steps.text: Spread the sliced meat back on the pan and broil 3 minutes. The little crispy edges are what the spit-man carves first — claim them.

steps.title: Build the wrap
steps.text: Warm the flatbread, spread toum generously, add meat, pickled onion, tomato and cucumber. Roll tight. Or serve as a plate over rice — the wrap is tradition, the plate is lunch tomorrow.

notes: Toum in 2 minutes: blitz 4 garlic cloves with lemon juice and salt, then drizzle in 150 ml neutral oil with the blender running until it mayonnaise-ifies. Add an ice cube if it splits.
Leftover roasted meat freezes well; reheat under the broiler to re-crisp.
The spice list looks long — it is one trip to a bulk spice bin and it lasts for months of shawarma.

storage: Marinated raw chicken keeps 2 days. Cooked meat 4 days refrigerated, 2 months frozen. Toum keeps a week refrigerated and gets hotter with age.

facts.origin: The Ottoman Levant — Bursa to Damascus to Beirut
facts.first_recorded: 1870s — the rotating vertical spit (döner) is invented in Bursa
facts.name_means: From Turkish çevirme, 'turning'. The Arabic word took the trip and stayed.
facts.technique: Layered yogurt-spice marinade, stacked roast, razor shavings
facts.season: Any — it is a street, streets do not close
facts.serve_at: Wrapped tight, eaten leaning over paper
facts.pour: Ayran — the salted yogurt drink that cools everything down

relations.cluster_note: Same idea, two empires: the rotating shaved roast (Ottoman) versus the lemon-oregano skewer (Greek).

similar.n: the street-wrap family: one plants, one shaves
